Let the rectangle have vertices \((0,0),(3,0),(3,1),(0,1)\). The internal angle bisectors are:

\[
y=x,\quad y=3-x,\quad y=x-2,\quad y=1-x.
\]

Their intersections give the quadrilateral vertices:

\[
\left(\frac32,\frac32\right),\quad \left(\frac52,\frac12\right),\quad \left(\frac32,-\frac12\right),\quad \left(\frac12,\frac12\right).
\]

Opposite-vertex distances (the diagonals) are:

\[
\left(\frac32,\frac32\right)\text{ to }\left(\frac32,-\frac12\right): 2,
\]
\[
\left(\frac52,\frac12\right)\text{ to }\left(\frac12,\frac12\right): 2.
\]

Thus the diagonals are both \(2\).

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
